topic: Revive parent stat_unknowncutoff_weaklate_frontier by characterizing and attaining the all-strength minimax expected length of connected honest intervals for fuzzy-RD LATE when both the compliance jump and unknown cutoff weaken. Preserve the parent’s binary, uniform-design, separate one-sided Hölder class. Replace its refuted affine moving-window localizer with certified support-wide marginal-likelihood profiling that retains unrestricted D-Y association. Derive the complete s=1 critical cutoff/effect-label experiment and decision value, an all-s total honest profile interval, and matching location-mixture and slope-kink converses. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A legal moving-cutoff continuum with q=1/4, c_t=1/2+t kappa/q, constant treatment-side jump kappa, affine outcome-side branches, independent observed D,Y, and an explicit monotone latent lift yields theta=t and KL(P_t^n,P_0^n)<=32 n kappa^3 |t|. This proves the missing min{1,1/(n kappa^3)} converse and 2[1-alpha-4 sqrt(n kappa^3)]_+ <= L_n* <= 2(1-alpha), so L_n* tends to 2(1-alpha) whenever n kappa^3 tends to zero; hence every fixed-s>1 location-entropy critical window is now exactly nonshrinking. The parent’s denominator-fallback containment was also repaired, and no collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a uniform profile-to-decision-value theorem with certified discretization, fallback, and calibration under unrestricted allowed D-Y association; solve the nontrivial s=1 critical window, its truncated mixture and second-order coordinates, and establish full-model least favorability on finite positive n kappa^3 faces. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the continuum causal lift, then solve increasingly fine certified whole-class population profile programs on both the parent’s affine counterexample and the new moving-cutoff family at s=1 and s=2; a persistent false-cutoff optimum or failure of the kappa^2|c-c'| gap stops that route. open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent controls only one side of the critical location-mixture experiment. At s=1, its first-order signal coordinate does not determine the limiting likelihood because boundary truncation, mixture renormalization, the signed effect label, and a second-order centering coordinate remain. Tuvaandorj supplies unknown-location experiment comparison for sharp RD, Elliott–Müller handle moderate unknown breaks, and Andrews–Mikusheva solve abstract weak-identification decisions, but none derives the joint binary fuzzy-RD cutoff/effect-label experiment or its connected-confidence-interval value. Composing those results does not establish experiment equivalence or least favorability under the target Hölder and causal restrictions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would prove Le Cam convergence to an explicit two-coordinate cutoff/effect-label experiment, characterize its fixed-α minimax expected-length value and least-favorable truncated mixture, and construct test-inverted connected intervals attaining that value uniformly on compact positive critical faces.

writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Plug-in location inference works for large jumps -> moderate jumps leave location nonregular -> uniform inference requires a process experiment -> solve the critical fuzzy-RD cutoff/effect-label decision problem

method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the direct bridge from indistinguishability in the limiting experiment to an attaining honest connected-interval value.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent refutes the deterministic separation inequality underlying its affine moving-window profile: the population objective can prefer a displaced false cutoff, so empirical-process bounds cannot repair that localizer. The transported-LATE score inversion works only with a scalar fixed-geometry moment, while an unknown cutoff requires a support-wide nuisance profile. Known-cutoff Anderson–Rubin inversion and conditional QLR theory do not provide the required Hölder-constrained continuum optimization, grid certificate, total fallback, or false-cutoff exclusion. Arai et al. further show why profiling independent D and Y marginals is insufficient: the procedure must retain the unrestricted joint cell law and its covariance information.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give a measurable joint-binary global profiling procedure with deterministic continuum-to-grid error bounds, uniform false-cutoff separation and localization tails, denominator fallback, calibrated cutoff/effect-label test inversion, honest coverage, and an all-strength expected-length limit or sharp bound.

method_exemplars.why_closest: An unknown cutoff produces a continuum-indexed process with a weakly identified nuisance mean, matching their functional-nuisance structure after deterministic profile separation is proved.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The repaired moving-cutoff continuum establishes the missing min{1,1/(nκ³)} obstruction near vanishing nκ³, but this tractable affine or independent subexperiment need not remain least favorable at finite positive signal. Known-cutoff modulus arguments perturb branches at a fixed boundary, whereas the full unknown-cutoff model admits both relocation of the compliance jump with compensating outcome branches and fixed-location slope or kink perturbations. Existing sharp-RD white-noise transfers neither preserve the binary monotone-compliance causal lift nor cover unrestricted D–Y association. A matching converse therefore requires legal alternatives in the unchanged class and a proof that no harder full-model direction enlarges the finite-face decision value.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would construct explicit monotone-lifted location-mixture and slope-kink experiments inside the full binary Hölder model and prove a finite-face lower bound matching the global profile’s expected-length value in every strength regime, or give a counterexample showing that the candidate frontier is not least favorable.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its decision-theoretic organization: derive a simpler experiment, prove its minimax lower bound, and transfer the result back while making the required model-preservation conditions explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unknown RD locations create a nonregular experiment -> simpler location models expose hard perturbations -> sharp RD yields localization converses -> fuzzy LATE requires causal-valid location mixtures plus slope-kink alternatives

method_exemplars.technique: Convert honest-coverage constraints into testing inequalities between modulus-attaining alternatives and integrate them into expected-length lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is an expected-length converse over a smoothness class; their testing-modulus duality supplies the final step once legal moving-cutoff alternatives are built.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt unknown-discontinuity white-noise lower-bound transfers to a joint binary treatment–outcome likelihood with drifting compliance strength.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its location experiment is the nearest analogue for the location-mixture half of the converse, but the causal lift and joint likelihood must be rebuilt.

method_exemplars.technique: Relate confidence-set expected length to integrated test power across weakly identified effect labels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The fuzzy-RD compliance jump is a local instrument-strength parameter, so its weak-identification length argument is the direct template for converting affinity across effect labels into an interval lower bound.

literature_map:
1. Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001, Econometrica) establish the standard known-cutoff sharp and fuzzy RD identification framework.
2. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016, JBES, DOI 10.1080/07350015.2015.1024836) show that a small first-stage jump invalidates conventional fuzzy-RD t inference.
3. Noack and Rothe (2024, Econometrica, arXiv:1906.04631) give bias-aware Anderson–Rubin-type fuzzy-RD confidence sets valid under weak identification, but retain a known cutoff.
4. Porter and Yu (2015, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2015.06.002) study unknown RD discontinuities mainly in a sharp design and a regime where cutoff estimation is asymptotically negligible for effect inference.
5. Tuvaandorj (2020, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.04.030) links sharp unknown-cutoff RD to a convolution white-noise experiment and obtains minimax location rates, not joint weak-fuzzy interval risk.
6. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2024, arXiv:2406.11585) propagate unknown-cutoff uncertainty through a Bayesian local/global RD model without frequentist honesty or all-strength minimax length.
7. Armstrong and Kolesár (2018, Econometrica, arXiv:1511.06028) derive finite-sample optimal honest intervals and modulus efficiency bounds for fixed-boundary linear functionals over convex smoothness classes.
8. Armstrong and Kolesár (2020, Quantitative Economics, arXiv:1606.01200) give nearly efficient honest nonparametric intervals, again for fixed-boundary functionals rather than a moving-cutoff ratio.
9. Moreira (2003), Andrews–Moreira–Stock (2006), and Mikusheva (2010) provide the conditional-likelihood, test-inversion, and expected-length analogies from weak-IV inference.
10. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, Econometrica, arXiv:1409.6337) develop uniformly valid conditional QLR inference with a functional nuisance parameter, a natural donor for cutoff-indexed profiling.
11. Andrews and Mikusheva (2022, Econometrica, arXiv:2007.04050) derive weak-GMM limit experiments and optimal decisions but do not solve the first-order Hölder moving-cutoff fuzzy-RD experiment.
12. Elliott and Müller (2014, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2014.03.007) show that moderate unknown breaks require a Gaussian-process limit experiment and invalidate uniform plug-in break-date inference.
13. Arai, Hsu, Kitagawa, Mourifié, and Wan (2022, Quantitative Economics, DOI 10.3982/QE1367) show that fuzzy-RD validity information lives in the joint outcome–treatment law, warning against marginal factorization.
14. Gerard, Rokkanen, and Rothe (2020, Quantitative Economics, DOI 10.3982/QE1079) derive manipulation-robust sharp bounds at a fixed known policy cutoff rather than a latent unknown cutoff with weak compliance.
15. Targeted searches found no paper jointly providing an unknown-cutoff weak-fuzzy-RD profile, an all-strength connected honest interval, its s=1 critical decision value, and matching finite-face expected-length converses.
